subject: Changing trajectory if present trajectory queue time is too long

messages.author: 84da51813582b567
messages.subject: Changing trajectory if present trajectory queue time is too long
parts:
Here is the code,

traj1 <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("res1", 1) %>%
  timeout(5)%>%
  release("res1", 1)

traj2 <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("res2", 1) %>%
  timeout(10)%>%
  release("res2", 1)
 
common_traj <- trajectory() %>%
  branch(option = function() sample(1:2, 1, prob = c(.5, .5)), continue = c(T,T),
         traj1,
         traj2 )

env <- mclapply(1:20, function(i) {
  simmer() %>%
    add_resource("res1", capacity = 1) %>%
    add_resource("res2", capacity = 1) %>%
    add_generator("high", traj2, from_to(0, 200, function() {10}), priority =1) %>%
    add_generator("low", common_traj, from_to(0, 200, function() (5))) %>%
    run(500)  %>%
    wrap()
})

If 'low' enters traj2 but res2 wait time is too long, can 'low' quite traj2 and enter traj1? I wasnt sure if rollback would work.
Kind regards,
